speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to our unit. I see you're a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; have you noticed any cyanosis or grunting breaths since birth? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT, CREATININE_PHOSPHOKINASE.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5; COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: NORMAL READINGS; CREATININE_PHOSPHOKINASE: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The presence of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a newborn is classic for RDS, likely due to surfactant deficiency; the previous suggestion of a urinary tract infection is inconsistent with this primary respiratory presentation. I will now request chest imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay.
